mascotLines: I never forget where I buried last year's bone. Checklists can finally carry over into a new season too.
I keep a leash pile AND a toy pile going without mixing them up. Clients can now hold more than one checklist too.
Old habits don't get grandfathered in forever — just ask any Desktop app still stuck before 4.8.1, now locked out for good.
I like my toys sorted into neat little piles. The Jobs page can now group itself by pipeline or stage, no sniffing required.

items.text: Reusable checklist templates for the whole firm
items.desc: Firms can now build named checklist templates — with a type, cadence, and document items — from a new Checklist templates tab in Settings, instead of rebuilding the same checklist from scratch for every client. Limited rollout.

items.text: A dedicated Checklists tab on the client Account page — and room for more than one checklist
items.desc: Client accounts now have an Organizers and checklists tab with separate Organizers and Checklists sub-tabs, where checklists can be created, edited, and deleted directly. This also lifts the old one-checklist-per-client limit, so a client can hold more than one checklist at a time — for example, one per tax type. Limited rollout.

items.text: Roll a client's checklist forward into a new period
items.desc: A new Roll over option lets firms carry a client's existing checklist items into a new checklist instead of rebuilding it by hand — available when creating or editing a checklist, and through pipeline automation. Limited rollout.

items.text: Roll over checklists when creating an organizer or bulk-importing
items.desc: The Roll over option is now also available where organizers get created — including for many client accounts at once — and bulk CSV/Excel imports gained a Rollover column, so firms don't have to open every account individually to carry a checklist forward. Limited rollout.

items.text: Organizer automation now attaches the right checklist automatically — and can AI-generate one
items.desc: When an organizer is created, either manually or through pipeline automation, TaxDome can now automatically work out and attach the matching checklist — reusing an existing one, rolling one forward, or creating one from a template — and can even generate checklist items straight from an uploaded 1040 with AI. Limited rollout.

items.text: One clear notification after any bulk checklist operation
items.desc: Rolling checklists forward, creating them from a template, or bulk-importing them now all produce the same kind of Inbox+ notification — showing how many were created, updated, or skipped, with a downloadable CSV for the details. Limited rollout.

items.text: Group the Jobs page by pipeline or by stage
items.desc: The Jobs page can now be grouped by pipeline or by stage, so admins can spot where work is piling up at a glance instead of filtering stage by stage. Limited rollout.

items.text: Older Desktop app versions are now blocked from signing in
items.desc: Desktop app versions from 4.1.0 up to (but not including) 4.8.1 had a bug that could send thousands of extra sync requests per hour. Those versions can no longer sign in, closing a loophole where the earlier force-update banner could be dismissed and ignored — so anyone still on an old version now needs to update to keep using the Desktop app.

items.text: Find AI form-exclusion settings right from Groups
items.desc: Firms using AI Groups can now jump straight to the form-exclusion preference settings from inside Groups itself, instead of hunting for them elsewhere — making it easier to stop the same forms from being pulled in automatically.

items.text: TRD: fix a disapproved return without rebuilding it
items.desc: When a client disapproves a Tax Return Delivery, firms currently have to build a whole new TRD from scratch. This is exploring a lighter way to correct and re-send just what needs fixing.

items.text: TRD: choose exactly who has to approve
items.desc: Right now, any contact with portal access can approve a Tax Return Delivery. This would let firms designate one specific approver instead.

items.text: TRD: require clients to confirm they reviewed a return before signing
items.desc: Exploring an explicit "I've reviewed this" confirmation step before e-signature, instead of relying on the signature itself as the only sign a client actually looked at the return.

items.text: A prebuilt Billing Monitor dashboard
items.desc: A ready-made dashboard for reviewing cash received, posted revenue, and what clients still owe — built for firm owners who currently export payments and AR to Excel to get this picture.

items.text: Employee cost rate
items.desc: Firms would be able to set a cost rate per employee and see job and client profitability right inside TaxDome, instead of exporting data and calculating margins by hand in spreadsheets.

items.text: Affirm or Klarna as a pay-over-time option
items.desc: Exploring adding a Buy Now, Pay Later option like Affirm or Klarna to TaxDome Payments, to make it easier for clients to pay larger invoices.

items.text: Bulk-create checklists from clients' existing documents
items.desc: Instead of building each client's document checklist by hand, this would generate checklists in bulk straight from documents clients have already uploaded.

items.text: Bulk-create checklists from a CSV
items.desc: Firms with a lot of clients to onboard at once would be able to generate document checklists for all of them in bulk from a CSV file, instead of one account at a time.

items.text: Desktop app: more reliable Drive syncing
items.desc: Ongoing work to make the Desktop app's Drive syncing more trustworthy, with clearer status and error messages when a sync fails instead of files just going missing quietly.

items.text: Desktop app: keeping up with high-volume tax prep firms
items.desc: Speed and bulk-upload improvements aimed at firms that process a high volume of returns, so the Desktop app doesn't slow them down during peak season.

items.text: Roll a checklist forward into the new season
items.desc: Carrying a client's prior-season checklist into the new season instead of losing all that context and rebuilding it from zero every year.

items.text: More than one checklist per client
items.desc: Today a new checklist overwrites the old one. This would let a firm keep several checklists per client at once — for example, one per tax type.

items.text: Fixed: clients could sign an autopay proposal with no payment method attached
items.desc: An unverified ACH bank account could be preselected on an autopay proposal and then silently removed before signing, letting a client complete signing with no payment method on file — leading to a confusing "Problem with payment" message later. Fixed so a payment method is always required before signing.

items.text: Fixed: the public sign-up page could fail with a server error
items.desc: A specific type of request to TaxDome's public sign-up page could return a server error instead of completing sign-up. Fixed.

items.text: Fixed: SMS two-factor setup could fail with a server error
items.desc: Setting up SMS-based two-factor authentication from TaxDome's general app subdomain (rather than a firm's own subdomain) could fail with a server error instead of completing. Fixed.

items.text: Fixed: one overly long file name could fail an entire document migration
items.desc: During document migration, if just one file in an uploaded folder had a very long file path, the whole folder's import would fail with a generic "Sync failed" error and no indication of which file caused it. Fixed.

items.text: Fixed: Portuguese (Brazil) language setting showed Norwegian text on some pages
items.desc: Firm members who set their interface language to Portuguese (Brazil) saw parts of the portal — including Billing — displayed in Norwegian instead. Fixed.

items.text: Fixed: an invoice created during document upload wasn't locked to that document
items.desc: When a firm user created and linked an invoice while uploading a document, the document uploaded successfully but wasn't actually locked to that invoice — with no error shown — requiring a manual re-link afterward. Fixed.

items.text: Fixed: a kiosk-only signer could sign outside of Kiosk Mode
items.desc: A signer meant only for in-office Kiosk Mode signing (someone with no email or login) could be used to sign a document even outside Kiosk Mode, bypassing the intended safeguard. Fixed.

poll.label: Roll over checklists into a new period (Beta)
Group Jobs by pipeline or stage (Beta)

mystery: This week's raw Jira pull touched 208 tickets — most of it backend refactors, test-pyramid cleanup, and a marketing-site redesign that'll never show up here. The Coming Soon board is also one item lighter: "Group the Jobs page by pipeline or stage" just graduated into Beta this week.
